name: Prasugrel
summary: A thienopyridine prodrug with faster, more consistent activation and greater platelet inhibition than clopidogrel — at the cost of higher bleeding risk.
mechanism: Prodrug requiring CYP-mediated activation (mainly CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP2C19) to an active metabolite that irreversibly blocks the platelet P2Y12 receptor.
pharmacodynamics: More rapid and potent platelet inhibition than clopidogrel; reduced ischemic events but increased major and fatal bleeding in ACS/PCI (TRITON-TIMI 38).

pharmacokinetics.metabolism: Hepatic activation (CYP3A4, CYP2B6, CYP2C19) then inactivation
pharmacokinetics.elimination: Renal (~68% as inactive metabolites) and fecal (~27%)

dosing.adult: Loading 60 mg, then 10 mg once daily (5 mg once daily if body weight <60 kg or age ≥75 years)
dosing.renalAdjustment: No dose adjustment for renal impairment (limited data in severe disease)

contraindications: History of TIA or stroke (increased intracranial hemorrhage)
warnings: Bleeding, including fatal intracranial hemorrhage — higher than clopidogrel
Do not use after prior TIA/stroke
monitoring: Complete blood count if bleeding suspected

indications: Acute coronary syndromes managed with PCI (with aspirin)
Reduction of thrombotic cardiovascular events in ACS/PCI patients
clinicalPearls: Activation is rapid and largely CYP2C19-independent — less pharmacogenetic variability than clopidogrel.
More potent than clopidogrel but contraindicated after TIA/stroke due to bleeding risk.
good: ACS patients undergoing PCI who need potent, irreversible antiplatelet effect.
bad: Patients with prior TIA/stroke, age ≥75 with low bleeding-risk tolerance, or low body weight.
